confirmed.title: AS-EFF-008 literal-masking is closed for Net only — Exec command / Fs path / Db table masking still certify a runtime-built forbidden endpoint
confirmed.location: surfaceIncomplete write site Candor.java:1934-1939 (guarded `if ("Net".equals(effect))`); the only other protection is the empty-surface failsafe in checkAllowlist at Candor.java:880 (`reached.isEmpty()`)
confirmed.mechanism: The masking fix (0.5.28/0.5.29) marks a method's surface INCOMPLETE when a Net reach has a structurally-invisible host (host-less owner or runtime-string host), so the gate fails closed even when a benign Net literal is also present. But `surfaceIncomplete` is populated at EXACTLY ONE site (Candor.java:1939) inside `if ("Net".equals(effect))` (line 1934). Exec, Fs and Db never populate it. For those three effects the only safeguard is the empty-surface failsafe `reached.isEmpty()` (line 880), which is per-method, not per-reach: a single benign captured literal makes `reached` non-empty and the gate certifies. So a method that performs `Runtime.exec("git status")` (captures cmds={git status}) AND `Runtime.exec(runtimeCmd)` (programHeadLiteral→null, no cmds captured, but Exec still emitted at Candor.java:4072) reaches an arbitrary attacker-controlled command yet passes `allow Exec git`. Identical for Fs (`new FileOutputStream("/var/app/data.log")` masks `new FileOutputStream(runtimePath)`) under `allow Fs /var/app`, and Db (`prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM accounts")` masks `prepareStatement(runtimeSql)`) under `allow Db accounts`. The benign co-literal MASKS the structurally-invisible runtime destination — exactly the Net evasion that was just fixed, left open for the other three injectable effects.
confirmed.trigger: One method that performs a host/cmd/path/table-establishing call with a BENIGN literal AND a second call of the same effect whose value is runtime-built (no static literal captured): e.g. `Runtime.getRuntime().exec("git status"); Runtime.getRuntime().exec(userSuppliedCmd);` gated by `allow Exec git`.
confirmed.why_real: Reproduced against the freshly built engine (build/install/candor-java/bin/candor-java). Exec: `CANDOR_POLICY=policy.candor candor-java cls` with `allow Exec git` over a method calling `Runtime.exec("git status")` then `Runtime.exec(userSuppliedCmd)` → `candor-java: no violations`, EXIT=0 (report shows inferred=[Exec], cmds=["git status"], no surfaceIncomplete). Control with ONLY the runtime command (no benign literal) → EXIT=1, `[AS-EFF-008] ... performs Exec with no visible literal — the surface cannot be certified`, proving the asymmetry is the benign literal masking. Fs variant (`allow Fs /var/app`, runtime path) → EXIT=0. Db variant (`allow Db accounts`, runtime SQL) → EXIT=0. All three certify a forbidden runtime endpoint; only Net fails closed.

confirmed.title: Package-granularity κ-classified flag whitewashes unmodeled sibling calls (silent under-disclosure)
confirmed.location: analyze() κ-ledger at line 1828-1833 (kappaSeen.merge / kappaClassified.add(pkg)) + globalBlind post-filter at line 4241-4243 / invisible computation at 4282-4284
confirmed.mechanism: The blind-spot ledger tracks coverage at PACKAGE granularity. When ANY call into an external package resolves to a classified κ rule (effect!=null), the WHOLE package is added to kappaClassified (line 1829). The global-blind set is then computed as `kappaSeen − kappaClassified` (line 4242), and `invisible` is the intersection of a fn's blindDirect reach with globalBlind (line 4283). So a single modeled method anywhere in the scan (e.g. org.jooq.DSLContext.fetch(String) → Db via isSqlBearingOwner) strips org.jooq from the blind set entirely, and every UNMODELED sibling method in that same package (org.jooq.DSLContext.settings(), floored to pure) is filtered out of blindDirect → emitted as plain pure with NO `invisible` field and NO κ-ledger warning. The disclosure floor silently stops applying to real blind reaches because an unrelated sibling happened to be modeled.
confirmed.trigger: In one scan: method A calls a modeled member of external pkg P (org.jooq.DSLContext.fetch(String)) AND method B calls an unmodeled member of the same pkg P (org.jooq.DSLContext.settings(), no String arg so isSqlBearingOwner misses → floored pure). B reads pure with no invisible disclosure.
confirmed.why_real: Reproduced with the 0.5.31-all jar. CONTROL (App2: only the opaque ctx.settings() call): stderr 'κ doesn't know 1 package... INVISIBLE (not Unknown): org.jooq (1 call)' and JSON `app.App2.runOpaque | inferred=[] | invisible=['org.jooq']` — honest. COMBINED (App / Trans: same opaque call PLUS a sibling calling the modeled ctx.fetch("x")): stderr emits NO invisible-package warning, and `runOpaque`/`opaque` is OMITTED entirely (plain pure, no invisible field) while only `runSql`/`classifiedSomewhere {Db}` is reported. The single classified sibling whitewashed the unmodeled sibling's blind reach across the whole scan.

confirmed.title: KAPPA_COVERED_PREFIXES blanket-declares whole namespaces 'modeled' — unmodeled members silent-pure, never disclosed
confirmed.location: KAPPA_COVERED_PREFIXES (line 3205-3207) + kappaCovers() (3209-3214) gating the ledger at line 1827

confirmed.title: AS-EFF-008 allowlist masking: a benign literal anywhere in the transitive closure certifies a function that also reaches a runtime/dynamic forbidden endpoint (Net/Exec/Fs/Db) — the candor-scan masking fix was never ported to the deep engine
confirmed.location: check_crate_post AS-EFF-008 block, lines ~3174-3231; decisive line `let opaque = reached.map(|set| set.is_empty()).unwrap_or(true);` (3207) and the gate condition `if !bad.is_empty() || opaque` (3208). Literal capture that produces the hole: net_hosts_in_call/first_str_lit_arg fed at lines 2486-2527 — a literal arg adds a host/cmd/path/table, a dynamic arg adds NOTHING.
confirmed.mechanism: The deep engine's allowlist gate computes the TRANSITIVE literal surface `reached` (hostsacc/cmdsacc/pathsacc/tablesacc) for the rule's effect, flags literals not covered (`bad`), and otherwise fails closed ONLY when that surface is completely empty (`opaque`). It has no per-method surface-incompleteness tracking. A Net/Exec/Fs/Db call whose destination is a runtime value (no string-literal arg) contributes NOTHING to `reached` (net_hosts_in_call / first_str_lit_arg return empty for a non-literal arg), so it is structurally invisible. If the same function transitively also reaches ONE allowlisted literal (e.g. a benign `TcpStream::connect("api.stripe.com:443")` via a helper), then `reached={api.stripe.com}`, `bad={}`, and `opaque=false` -> the function is CERTIFIED while transitively reaching the forbidden runtime endpoint. The benign literal MASKS the invisible reach. This is the exact evasion candor-scan closed in commit 52191b0 via per-fn `incomplete`/`surface_incomplete` propagation, but that fix was applied to crates/candor-scan/src/main.rs ONLY — the deep (sole-sound) engine src/lib.rs was never updated (memory's own note: 'the SAME masking in candor-rust/ts/swift ... coordinated cross-engine port recommended'). The deep engine is also WORSE than scan's fix here: scan's fix is Net-only, but the deep engine masks all four literal-bearing effects (Net/Exec/Fs/Db).
confirmed.trigger: A scoped `allow Net in billing api.stripe.com` (or Exec/Fs/Db equivalent). A public fn `charge(h: String)` that calls a helper performing a captured benign literal effect (`TcpStream::connect("api.stripe.com:443")`) AND a helper performing the same effect on a runtime value (`TcpStream::connect(h)` / `Command::new(prog)` / `fs::read(p)`). The pure-opaque leaf helper is flagged, but the mixed-surface caller `charge` certifies green.
confirmed.why_real: REPRODUCED on the freshly-built dylib (libcandor@nightly-2026-04-16). Net: with `allow Net in billing api.stripe.com`, `billing::charge` (calls ping_stripe -> connect("api.stripe.com:443") AND exfil(host) -> connect(host)) produced ZERO AS-EFF-008 warnings (grep -c = 0); removing only the benign ping_stripe() call made `billing::charge` immediately flag `performs Net to a host candor cannot determine` — proving the benign literal is load-bearing in suppressing the warning. Exec: `ci::deploy` (run_git()->Command::new("git") + run_dynamic(prog)->Command::new(prog)) NOT flagged under `allow Exec in ci git` while reaching `Command::new("/bin/sh")`-class arbitrary exec; only the leaf run_dynamic flagged. Fs: `config::load` NOT flagged under `allow Fs in config /etc/app` while transitively reading `/etc/shadow` via fs::read(runtime_path); only the leaf read_dynamic flagged. In every case the entry/boundary function that a CI gate actually checks certifies green while reaching a forbidden, runtime-controlled endpoint.

confirmed.title: Deep (sound) engine never populates `invisible` — unmodeled-crate floor is silent: pure with no per-fn disclosure, no Unknown, no κ-ledger
confirmed.location: Candor::check_crate_post JSON emit, ReportEntry construction at src/lib.rs:3005 (`invisible: Vec::new()` hardcoded); the floor itself at the `else if !def_id.is_local() { ... if self.cross.is_empty() { return; } }` branch, src/lib.rs:2539-2559
confirmed.mechanism: When the deep engine resolves a call into a non-local crate the curated classifier does not model (`classify`/`classify_extra` return None) and no sibling report is loaded (`self.cross.is_empty()`), it `return`s recording NO effect and NO `Unknown` — the advisory floor. That floor is acceptable BY DESIGN only if disclosed. The scan engine discloses it via the per-fn `invisible` field (commit 77f2f82) and a stderr κ-ledger. The deep engine — positioned in AGENTS.md as "the sound gate" / "the only SOUND engine" — was NOT updated by that commit: every ReportEntry it emits hardcodes `invisible: Vec::new()`, it prints no κ-ledger, and (worse than scan, which keeps a pure-but-blind row) it DROPS the pure function from `functions` entirely. The blind crate IS captured in `self.encountered` and written to an `encountered-*.json` sidecar, but that is not the report's per-fn `invisible` field, is not filtered to genuinely-unclassified crates, and is invisible to the AGENTS.md trust contract (which reads `inferred:[]` + empty `invisible` as an honest pure claim). So a fn reaching a blind module reads plainly pure with zero honesty caveat — undisclosed under-disclosure (lens b/c), propagating transitively to all callers. Consequence: a `deny Fs` policy on the sound engine PASSES (exit 0) for a fn that performs Fs through the unmodeled crate, with no signal a floor was applied.
confirmed.trigger: A function `handler()` in crate `consumer` that calls `mysteryio::write_secret()` where `mysteryio` is any crate not in candor-classify's CALIBRATED set and not a workspace sibling (so no report is chained). `mysteryio::write_secret` does real `std::fs` I/O.

The `encountered-consumer-Rlib.json` sidecar holds `["mysteryio"]` but the report's per-fn disclosure is silent. The SAME fixture under the scan engine emits `{"fn":"handler","inferred":[],"invisible":["mysteryio"]}` plus stderr `κ doesn't know 1 dependency this code calls into ... mysteryio (1 call)` — proving the disclosure is expected and that the sound engine regressed relative to the advisory one. A `deny Fs handler` policy on the deep engine returned EXIT=0 (clean pass) for the Fs-performing fn, undisclosed. grep confirms `invisible` appears in src/lib.rs only at line 3005 as `Vec::new()`; commit 77f2f82 (`feat(scan,report): ... invisible field`) did not touch src/lib.rs.

confirmed.title: sea_orm `::all`/`::count` execution-verb rule fabricates Db on the pure sea_query builder algebra (Func::count, Condition::all, Expr::count)
confirmed.location: classify(), sea_orm branch lines 665-684 (`path.ends_with("::all")`, `path.ends_with("::count")`)

confirmed.title: Free-fn aliased through a `let` binding then called is silently pure (effect + whole transitive chain dropped)
confirmed.location: visit_local else-branch (lines ~1343-1358) feeds fn-aliasing; visit_expr_call Path arm (lines ~1093-1106) drops the call
confirmed.mechanism: `let g = eff;` where `eff` is a visible free fn: in visit_local the init is an `Expr::Path` that is NOT in `fn_typed_vars` (that set only holds params/locals declared with an `Fn`/`fn` type), so `expr_is_fn_typed` is false; `ctor_type` returns None for a fn-path, so `g` is recorded as nothing. At the call site `g()`, `g` is neither in `fn_typed_vars` nor `closure_vars`, so visit_expr_call treats it as a phantom call to a free fn literally named `g`, which resolves to no target and is dropped — NOT marked Unknown. The engine actively tracks fn-aliasing for the Unknown-callback case but misses a path-to-a-known-fn, so the named target's effect is neither resolved (the deep/nightly engine DOES add this caller->fn edge per BACKLOG line 191-201 'the statically-resolvable half is closed') nor disclosed as Unknown. Reproduced: `pub fn inner(){ let g = eff; g(); } pub fn outer(){ inner(); }` with `eff` doing std::fs::read — candor-scan emits ONLY `eff:[Fs]`; both `inner` and `outer` are absent from the report (= certified pure, not Unknown). The whole transitive chain reads network/fs-free when it is not, and the README only claims honest Unknown for fn-pointers held in a field/dispatch-table/index, so this let-alias case is an UNDISCLOSED silent-pure.
confirmed.trigger: pub fn eff(){ std::fs::read("x").unwrap(); } pub fn inner(){ let g = eff; g(); }
confirmed.why_real: Reproduced with candor-scan 0.5.3 (target/release/candor-scan). Direct `inner(){ eff(); }` correctly yields [Fs]; the aliased `let g = eff; g();` yields NO entry for inner (pure), and a caller `outer` of it is also pure. Wrong output: report contains only `eff [Fs]`, inner+outer silently absent/pure (not Unknown).

confirmed.title: Literal-MASKING defeats the AS-EFF-008 allowlist for ALL four effects (Net/Fs/Exec/Db): a benign allowed literal hides an invisible runtime-controlled endpoint and the gate certifies clean
confirmed.location: AS-EFF-008 allowlist enforcement, fn check_crate gate loop, src/lib.rs:3208 (the `opaque = reached.map(|set| set.is_empty())` failsafe) + literal capture at net_hosts_in_call (1748) / first_str_lit_arg (1771)
confirmed.mechanism: The gate's only fail-closed failsafe for an un-pinnable destination is `opaque = reached_surface.is_empty()`. `reached` is the TRANSITIVE UNION of literals seen at classified effect calls (hostsacc/cmdsacc/pathsacc/tablesacc). A call to a host-/path-/command-establishing API with a RUNTIME argument (e.g. TcpStream::connect(runtime_host), fs::read(runtime_path), Command::new(arg)) contributes NOTHING to that union — net_hosts_in_call / first_str_lit_arg silently return empty and leave no incompleteness marker. So a function that performs BOTH (a) a benign call with an allowed literal arg AND (b) an establishing call with a runtime arg ends up with a non-empty surface containing only the benign literal. `opaque` is then false, every reached literal is allowed so `bad` is empty, and the function CERTIFIES — even though it reaches a fully attacker/runtime-controlled endpoint. This is exactly the per-method `surfaceIncomplete` masking that candor-java fixed in 0.5.29; the Rust nightly gate has no equivalent per-establishing-call incompleteness flag, only the union-emptiness check. Not in this repo's BACKLOG.md.
confirmed.trigger: A scoped allow rule (e.g. `allow Net in billing api.stripe.com`) + a function in scope that does `TcpStream::connect("api.stripe.com:443"); TcpStream::connect(runtime_host);` — generalizes to `allow Fs … /etc/app` with `fs::read_to_string("/etc/app/cfg.toml"); fs::read_to_string(runtime_path);` and `allow Exec … git` with `Command::new("git")…; Command::new(arg)…`.
confirmed.why_real: Reproduced with the built nightly dylib (libcandor@nightly-2026-04-16). MASKED case (benign literal + runtime connect): 0 AS-EFF-008 warnings — CERTIFIED. CONTROL (runtime connect ONLY, benign literal removed): 1 warning: `[AS-EFF-008] \`billing::charge\` performs Net to a host candor cannot determine (a dynamically-built value); the allowlist cannot be certified`. The sole difference is the presence of one allowed literal, which flips `opaque` false. Confirmed identical evasion for Fs (`config::load` reads an arbitrary runtime path) and Exec (`ci::run` runs an arbitrary runtime command): both certify with 0 warnings.

confirmed.title: `invisible` blind-reach disclosure is silently dropped across the CANDOR_DEPS cross-crate join (under-disclosure at the chain boundary)
confirmed.location: DepFn struct (line 224-231) + dep-report parser (lines 302-327) + the join at lines 3261-3270

confirmed.location: KAPPA_RULES, the net-cluster rule [/^(node:)?(net|dgram|tls|http2?|https)$/, /^(?!(new|isIP|isIPv4|isIPv6)$)/, "Net"] (line 42); applied in scan.mjs kappa() at the (CLASSIFY) site line 994

confirmed.title: Effectful setter dropped on compound/logical assignment (`obj.prop += v`, `??=`, `||=`, `&&=`) when the getter is pure → caller reads PURE
confirmed.location: visitCalls, accessor-access arm, lines 1163-1178 (the `isAssignTarget` test at line 1168-1169)
confirmed.mechanism: The accessor dispatch decides setter-vs-getter with `isAssignTarget = p.operatorToken.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.EqualsToken`. Only a *simple* `=` assignment is treated as a setter site. A compound assignment (`+=`,`-=`,`*=`, etc.) and a logical assignment (`??=`,`||=`,`&&=`) all have a non-`EqualsToken` operator on the LHS property access, so `isAssignTarget` is false and the code resolves the GETTER (`accessorAt(node,"get")`) instead of the setter. These forms genuinely INVOKE the setter at runtime (`x.prop += v` ≡ `x.prop = x.prop + v`; `x.prop ??= v` writes when nullish). When the getter is pure but the setter is effectful (the everyday read/write-through accessor pair — a persisting counter, a config that flushes on set, a cache that writes on assign), the engine edges only to the pure getter and the setter's effect is never reached. The result is omitted entirely from the report (concrete-pure, not even Unknown). The inline comment even acknowledges `x.prop += v` 'is both a read and a write' but deliberately models only the read side — the write side (the effect) is dropped. Both PropertyAccess and ElementAccess (`c["count"] += 1`) are affected.
confirmed.trigger: class C { get count(){return this.#n;} set count(v){ fs.appendFileSync(p,v);} }  export function bump(c:C){ c.count += 1; }  // also c.count ??= x, c.count ||= x, c["count"] += 1
confirmed.why_real: Reproduced with node scan.mjs. Fixture /tmp/cf6 (pure getter `count`, effectful setter doing fs.appendFileSync): `bump(c){ c.count += 1 }` => report OMITS the function ('bump => PURE/omitted'); the setter unit itself is correctly `a.Store.set count ["Fs"]` but the caller never edges to it. /tmp/cf3 confirms `viaNullish` (`??=`), `viaOr` (`||=`) and `viaCompound` (`+=`) are all omitted while only `viaPlain` (`=`) catches the setter (report shows just `a.Store.set config [Fs]` + `a.viaPlain [Fs]`). /tmp/cf7 confirms element-access `c["count"] += 1` is likewise dropped. Gate-evasion implication: a `deny Fs`/`forbid Fs` §6.2 policy passes on code that writes a file via `obj.prop += x`.

confirmed.title: Policy parser: bare-CR (classic-Mac) line endings silently drop every rule after the first (Rust/TS/Swift); Java splits correctly — gateless-green divergence
confirmed.location: parse_policy() — line iteration uses `text.lines()` (splits on \n / \r\n only, NOT bare \r), while `\r` IS in `is_ascii_ws` so it is then treated as an in-line TOKEN separator
confirmed.mechanism: A CANDOR_POLICY file saved with bare-CR line endings (e.g. `deny Net domain\rdeny Exec\rforbid domain -> infra\r`) is read by `std::fs::read_to_string` un-normalized. `text.lines()` does not split on a bare `\r`, so the whole file is ONE logical line. Then `line.split(is_ascii_ws)` (which includes `\r`) tokenizes it as `deny Net domain deny Exec forbid domain -> infra`. The `deny` branch reads `Net` then hits the first non-effect token `domain`, sets scope=domain, and STOPS — every subsequent rule (`deny Exec`, `forbid domain -> infra`) is swallowed as trailing tokens and discarded. Net result: a multi-rule policy collapses to its first rule. Java instead reads lines via `Files.readAllLines`, which DOES split on bare `\r`, so Java parses all three rules. TS (policy.mjs: `text.split("\n")` + `ASCII_WS` regex includes `\r`) and Swift (main.swift: `split(separator:"\n")` + tokenizer `{ $0.isASCII && $0.isWhitespace }` treats `\r` as a separator) behave identically to Rust. So the same policy file means DIFFERENT things across engines: under Rust/TS/Swift a project-wide `deny Exec` ban and a `forbid` layering rule vanish (gate goes silently green on a forbidden Exec / forbidden layer edge); under Java they are enforced. No reader normalizes CR in any engine.

confirmed.title: Effectful setter dropped when a property setter is a destructuring-assignment target (`({k: obj.prop} = src)`)
confirmed.location: visitCalls, accessor-access arm, lines 1163-1178 — `isAssignTarget` only recognizes a BinaryExpression `=` whose `left===node`, not a property access nested inside an assignment Object/Array literal pattern

confirmed.title: Prefix/postfix operator overloads are silent-pure (only infix operators get an edge)
confirmed.location: CallCollector.visit(SequenceExprSyntax) at lines 1249-1280 — operator resolution only matches BinaryOperatorExprSyntax; there is NO visitor for PrefixOperatorExprSyntax / PostfixOperatorExprSyntax
confirmed.mechanism: SwiftParser leaves operators unfolded. The engine resolves operator overloads exclusively inside the SequenceExpr visitor, which iterates looking for `BinaryOperatorExprSyntax` (infix) operands and edges to `<Type>.<op>` / the free `<op>` unit. A prefix application `~>x` is a PrefixOperatorExprSyntax and a postfix `x<!>` is a PostfixOperatorExprSyntax — neither is a SequenceExpr and no visitor walks them. The custom operator FUNCTION body is analyzed (it appears in the report with its real effect), but the caller never gets an edge to it, so a caller that invokes an effectful local prefix/postfix operator reads silently pure.
confirmed.trigger: `prefix func ~> (x: W) { x.boom() /* Fs */ }` then `func usePrefix(w: W) { ~>w }` — or the postfix twin `postfix func <!>(x: W){x.boom()}` ; `func f(w: W){ w<!> }`

But `usePrefix`/`usePrefix2`/`usePostfix` were ABSENT from the report (pure) with empty callgraph edges (`usePrefix edges: []`), while the operator units `~> ['Fs']`, `=> ['Fs']`, `<!> ['Fs']` were present with their effect. So the effectful prefix/postfix operator's effect is dropped at every call site.

confirmed.title: Rust models DNS only at the libc getaddrinfo layer — the idiomatic stdlib `std::net::ToSocketAddrs::to_socket_addrs` / `std::net::lookup_host` DNS resolve floors silently
confirmed.location: classify() std::net branch (lines 539-547) matches only `std::net::TcpStream`/`TcpListener`/`UdpSocket`; there is no rule for `std::net::ToSocketAddrs::to_socket_addrs` or `std::net::lookup_host`. Java/TS model the equivalent host→address resolution directly (InetAddress.getByName / node:dns); Rust only catches it if the user drops to raw libc::getaddrinfo, which idiomatic Rust never does. This is the same DNS-resolution op the siblings classify, missed at Rust's most common spelling. It is also not disclosed: the scan emits an empty report (no `invisible`, no ledger entry) because `std` is the platform, not a third-party floor.
confirmed.trigger: use std::net::ToSocketAddrs; pub fn resolve(h: &str) -> bool { (h, 80).to_socket_addrs().is_ok() }  // DNS resolve, reads PURE
